Severe dysautonomia in glycine receptor antibody-positive
progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus
(PERM): A case report
Yasuaki Mizutani e Shunsuke Adachi e Shoko Nakano e ... Akihiro Ueda e Mizuki Ito e
Hirohisa Watanabe & e Show all authors
Published: November 15, 2021 ® DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autneu.2021.102910 ® Check for updates
“ PlumX Metrics
Highlights
e PERM is a disorder causing progressive encephalomyelitis, rigidity, and myoclonus.
iutonomia has been described in PERM but its mechanism remains unclear.
= ¢

¢ Severe dysautonomia developed in a case of PERM with glycine receptor antibodies.
¢ Dysautonomia was presumed due to antibody-mediated sympathetic hyperactivity.
¢ Alpha-blocker may be useful for immunotherapy-resistant autoimmune dysautonomia.
Abstract
Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM) is a severe form of stiff-person
spectrum disorder. We report a 59-year-old man who presented with progressive encephalomyelitis
causing diplopia, bulbar palsy, severe dysautonomia, followed by stiffness and myoclonic cluster.
Laboratory tests showed mild pleocytosis, with markedly elevated plasma levels of norepinephrine,
epinephrine, and arginine vasopressin. Glycine-receptor antibodies were identified in both serum
and CSF. Despite a poor response to methylprednisolone, immunoglobulins, and plasma exchange,
a-blocker stabilized dysautonomia. Dysautonomia is presumed to be due to antibody-mediated
disinhibited sympathetic hyperactivity; however, this case suggests that concomitant use of a-
blocker with immunotherapy may ameliorate dysautonomia.
